title: NWP Device Schemas
description: Per-category device schemas matching the ERD's class-table-inheritance structure: a shared Device core plus one subtype block per hardware category. Composed via allOf so each category schema is core Device fields + its own specs.

coreDevice.description: Fields common to every device row, regardless of category — matches the Device table.

price.description: Unit price. null = unknown/price on request (excluded from Cost-Efficient ranking); 0 = genuinely free.

product_line.description: Name of the product line this device belongs to. The seed script resolves it to Device.product_line_id by matching (vendor_id, category, name) against product_lines.json, and the catalog export flattens that line's line_rank and name onto the CatalogSku. Required for gateway_router, ap and switch devices, because the High-Performance plan picks its SKU from the next line up (by line_rank) compared with the Cost-Efficient plan. Omit for controllers, racks and standalone firewalls.

capabilities.description: Role tags written to the DeviceCapability junction at seed time (capability_desc values; the seed script resolves each to a capability_id). Fixed vocabulary so a typo can't create a new capability. Tag every role a multi-role device performs so the engine knows it replaces separate devices. Optional for single-role devices.

sfp_ports.description: Number of SFP-family ports. A subset of wan_ports + lan_ports, not additional to it.

sfp_form_factor.description: Form factor of the SFP ports. Required when sfp_ports > 0.

sfp_ports.description: Number of SFP-family ports. A subset of the total port count, not additional to it.

sfp_form_factor.description: Form factor of the SFP ports. Required when sfp_ports > 0.

firewallSpecs.description: Firewall specifications table. Used standalone for dedicated firewall devices, and optionally nested under a gateway/router entry when that device is also capability-tagged as a firewall (see DeviceCapability junction, e.g. UDM-Pro).

controllerSpecs.description: Controller specifications table. A purchasable hardware controller appliance (e.g. Omada OC200/OC300-style) or a licensed cloud/software controller line item. Selected by the engine when the chosen vendor has need_controller = true; sizing is checked per device type: planned AP, switch and gateway counts must each fit within max_managed_aps / max_managed_switches / max_managed_gateways.

controller_type.description: hardware = standalone physical appliance; software = self-hosted install; cloud = vendor-hosted (typically licensed); integrated = built into another device (e.g. a router such as the Omada ER7212PC) and not separately purchasable.

max_managed_aps.description: Max access points this controller can manage.

max_managed_switches.description: Max switches this controller can manage.

max_managed_gateways.description: Max gateways/routers this controller can manage.

max_managed_aps_and_switches.description: Optional combined cap shared by access points and switches, for controllers whose vendor states one (e.g. 22 for the Omada ER7212PC's integrated controller). The engine checks aps + switches against this in addition to the per-type limits.

lan_ports.description: Ethernet ports on the appliance. Use 0 or omit for software/cloud controllers.

sfpFormFactor.description: Physical SFP-family form factor of a switch or gateway port. SFP modules themselves are not catalogued; they appear on the Installation Materials Summary.

firewall_specs.description: Present only when this gateway/router is ALSO capability-tagged as a firewall (dual-role device, e.g. UniFi UDM-Pro). Omit entirely for a plain gateway with no firewall role — don't send null, just leave the key out.

switch_specs.description: Present only when this gateway/router has an integrated switch (e.g. Omada ER7212PC with built-in PoE ports). Omit entirely for a plain gateway. The engine counts ports from this block, so gateway_router_specs.lan_ports must be 0 whenever switch_specs is present (enforced below).

controller_specs.description: Present only when this gateway/router has an integrated controller (e.g. Omada ER7212PC). Omit entirely for a plain gateway.

firewallDevice.description: A dedicated, standalone firewall device (e.g. a Reyee RG-WALL 1600-equivalent) — not a gateway with firewall capability layered on. Multi-role devices belong under gatewayRouterDevice instead, with firewall_specs nested there.

controllerDevice.description: A network controller (hardware appliance, self-hosted software, or cloud license). Only relevant for vendors with need_controller = true. Controllers are chosen by sizing, not by product line, so product_line is omitted.
